description: The 20 consolidated anti-patterns (founding doc section 12), one atom each, numbered in payloads. Encoded LAST-but-one so their constrains/derived_from edges can target the procedures and facts from batches 02-08. Hub: hub_sf_antipatterns. 3-segment names are deliberate conflict gates: a future claim of the opposite value must collide.

atoms.payload: [V-M] Anti-pattern 1: never locate by generated ids (#input-42, Aura globalIds like 940:1376;a) — they regenerate every render and are per-component-scoped under native shadow. Use role/label/text first, API-name attributes second.

[V-O] Anti-pattern 2: no XPath at all on Salesforce UI — structurally brittle AND blind to shadow roots. It works on LEX today only through the synthetic-shadow accident and will silently return zero matches as subtrees flip to native shadow.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 3: ban waitForTimeout and all fixed sleeps; every wait must name the app-visible condition it awaits (spinner count 0, toast visible, dialog hidden, heading rendered). Sleeps are simultaneously too slow (pad green runs) and too short (flake under load).

[V-M] Anti-pattern 4: never create test data through the UI — slow, flaky, and couples every journey to the create forms. Seed via API (jsforce / REST / Composite Tree), deep-link to the record, use the UI only for the behavior under test.
[V-M] Anti-pattern 5: never hardcode record ids — they are org-specific and environment-fragile. Create records per run or resolve ids by query at runtime, and pass them through refs/fixtures.

[V-O] Anti-pattern 6: one dedicated test user per parallel worker — a user shared across workers collides on server-side state (record locks, list views, recents, personal settings) and produces unreproducible flake.

[S] Anti-pattern 7: run each test under the profile/persona it claims to test — rendering is role-based (FlexiPages, audience targeting, permissions), so admin-run tests validate an admin UI that real users never see.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 8: pin test-user timezone and locale, and compute expected values from THEM — Salesforce stores UTC and renders per-user. Deriving expectations from the CI machine clock/locale is a latent off-by-a-day and number-format bug.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 9: log in once and reuse the session (token injection + storageState) — the single biggest speed and flake win. Per-test UI login is banned except when the login experience itself is the thing under test.

[S] Anti-pattern 10: secrets live in vault/CI secrets/.env (git-ignored) — never hardcoded in specs, personas.json, or committed config. personas.json carries env-var NAMES only (usernameEnv); values are resolved at setup time.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 11: every created record carries a unique run prefix (E2E_<runid>_...) and a periodic API sweeper deletes strays from crashed runs. Unique naming makes parallel runs collision-safe and makes cleanup queryable.

[S] Anti-pattern 12: assert both sides — UI state AND persisted API/SOQL state. A success toast can lie: validation rules and async processes can revert or block the save after the toast renders. UI-only assertions are insufficient for any state-changing action.

[S/V-M] Anti-pattern 13 (omission): add accessibility checks (@axe-core/playwright) and visual regression to the suite — seasonal releases change rendering without breaking function, and SLDS 2 introduces theme variance. Keep visual baselines per theme.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 14 (expectation): expect Visualforce iframes inside Lightning pages — cross-origin frames with classic DOM. Reach them with frameLocator; treating frame content as missing page content is a diagnosis error.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 15: locators live in exactly one place (page object or component object) and maintenance is budgeted for 3 Salesforce releases/year. Scattered duplicate locators turn each release into a suite-wide hunt.
[V-O] Anti-pattern 16: assert toasts immediately after the triggering action — platform toasts auto-dismiss at 4.8s (9.6s with a link); any intervening step makes the toast assertion a race.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 17: scope locators to containers (dialog, tabpanel, row) — Salesforce repeats labels and button names across page regions; unscoped locators either throw strict-mode violations or silently hit the wrong region's control.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 18: on portals, run the same spec under EVERY persona and assert presence AND absence — persona-conditional rendering plus silent-empty guest failures mean a portal is only proven when unauthorized personas are shown NOT to see/do things. Absence assertions are the anti-gaming half of portal coverage.

[V-M] Anti-pattern 19: a locator failure is often a permissions/config failure in disguise — check profile, permission sets, and FlexiPage assignment BEFORE rewriting the selector; the element may genuinely not exist for that user.

[V-O] Anti-pattern 20: treat maintenance / Service Not Available pages as first-class assertion targets so infrastructure states fail with a precise message ('site is down') instead of masquerading as element-not-found three steps later.
